How can I change only the color of a vase in a photo using an AI image editing prompt? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
To change only the color of a vase in a photo using an AI image editing prompt, you should use a generative fill or inpainting AI editor, specify the object precisely, and explicitly describe the targeted color change while instructing the tool to keep the rest of the image untouched.
Here is the exact step-by-step process used by modern AI image modifiers to successfully recolor isolated elements:
1. Upload Your Photo to an Inpainting AI Tool
Choose an AI editor capable of selective object modification. Platforms like the PixelBin AI Recolor Tool or Kling AI allow you to easily upload standard image formats like JPG, JPEG, PNG, or WEBP. 
Kling AI
 +1
2. Isolate the Vase (If Using Brush Selection)
Many advanced AI interfaces offer a manual selection or brush tool. If available, highlight or "mask" over the vase to tell the AI exactly where to focus. This step acts as a "visual prompt" that ensures the background, flowers, or surrounding furniture remain perfectly intact. 
Canva
 +2
3. Write a Specific, Targeted Text Prompt
When writing your prompt, keep it concise but descriptive. Long, complex sentences can confuse the AI. Avoid modifying the whole image; specify both the target object and the new color. 
YouTube
·Magnific
 +2
Good Prompt Structure: "Change the color of the vase to sapphire blue, keeping the texture and surrounding scene identical."
Alternative Prompt Structure: "A ceramic vase recolored to matte emerald green."
4. Generate and Refine
Click generate and let the AI process the image, which typically takes anywhere from a few seconds to a minute depending on the model. If the editor supports model selections like those found in the Piktochart AI Image Modifier, using an advanced model like GPT Image 2 will yield highly realistic shading and lighting on your newly colored object. Once satisfied, preview the results and download your newly edited photo.
